html:
The World Nomad Games are an international sports festival of the traditional games of Central Asia and other steppe peoples. The first games were held in 2014 at Cholpon-Ata, on the shore of Lake Issyk-Kul in Kyrgyzstan.

Kyrgyzstan hosted the first three, in 2014, 2016 and 2018. Turkey held the fourth at Iznik in 2022, and Astana in Kazakhstan the fifth in 2024, with athletes from about ninety countries.

The sports come from the life of herders and horsemen:

  • Kok boru, a rough team game on horseback played with a goat carcass, like the Afghan buzkashi.
  • Wrestling on foot and on horseback.
  • Horse racing over long distances, and archery from horseback.
  • Hunting with eagles and falcons.
  • Board games such as toguz korgool.

The games are a show of national pride for the new Central Asian states and celebrate a nomadic heritage that Soviet rule tried to erase, much like Naadam in Mongolia.
